title: The Four Factions of Fein Uaill
type: A guide to Zarathis’s shared institutions
dek: Four ways of serving the same land: preserving its memory, cultivating knowledge, seeking freedom and tending the living world.
tags: The Four Factions of Fein Uaill

chapters.title: What each brings to the same society
Their leaders and their public representatives

body:
Zarathis’s factions are part of how people live together: work, protection, learning, ambition and care for the land. They share a home without sharing every answer. The following histories follow their stated ideals into the scenes where those ideals are practiced, disputed or strained.

Meet the four factions

The Order of the Silver StarSoldiers, historians and craftspeople who defend Zarathis by carrying its past into the present—and must decide what preserving it requires.The Council of the Emerald VeilThe Council behind libraries, careful briefings and ambitious arcane research, whose promise of safety repeatedly meets the risks of discovery and war.The Legion of the Radiant FlameA legion of warriors and explorers seeking lives of their own making, with a shared flame that becomes painfully contested when its dead return.The Verdant CircleThe keepers of grove and garden, whose work joins healing and cultivation to hard questions about intervention, research and the boundary of life.

What each brings to the same society

The Silver Star carries the past forward through defense, historical memory and craft. The Emerald Veil cultivates knowledge, diplomacy and the material arrangements of a flourishing city. The Radiant Flame pursues freedom, exploration and courage expressed in action. The Verdant Circle tends the land and the living systems on which every other pursuit depends.

These are distinctions of purpose, not four sealed populations. A mason consults a druid before changing a river. Scholars and warriors take part in the same dangerous expedition. A faction can endorse someone associated with another, or someone who says she belongs to none. Míriel’s cultural tour deliberately introduces ordinary people: an account made only of leaders and contests would miss much of the society.

Their leaders and their public representatives

The faction descriptions name Lord-Captain Tyragol for the Silver Star, Lord Aldamir Silvertaine for the Emerald Veil, High Lady Liraeth Dawnbringer for the Radiant Flame, and Archdruid Thalindra Were-sage for the Verdant Circle. Each subsequently appears as a faction speaker in the leadership nominations after Aria’s death.

Tarwen, Míriel, Arandiel and Mîrwen are also important public representatives. Their appearances do not erase the named faction leaders or supply a full institutional chart. Bowene’s civic office and Aria’s stature as a cultural leader and great commander belong alongside these institutions. They should not be collapsed into one interchangeable position.

In the nomination scene, the Silver Star backs Wren, the Emerald Veil backs Magnus, the Radiant Flame backs Arandiel and the Verdant Circle backs Lucent. Bowene later says that he, the council of four and Magnus have work to do. The record does not require every one of their powers or jurisdictions to be reconstructed from that remark.

Where cooperation becomes disagreement

The dam joins Silver Star construction to Verdant Circle advice; the Void expedition joins Silver Star and Emerald Veil scholarship to Radiant Flame forces, with the Circle repairing damage it is said to oppose. These encounters show cooperation without erasing disagreement.

The memorial makes the differences painful. Silver Star care for burial and Radiant Flame rites for the spirit meet Elenia’s willingness to restore the dead through divine power. The returned soldiers do not automatically resolve what their return means to their people. Arandiel’s tears, Magnus’s demand for consequences and Elenia’s later exile carry the disagreement forward.
